pool.text: Rescue lifeboat established after wreck of HMS Brazen.
First Newhaven Lifeboat commissioned, among Britain’s oldest.
Railway arrival increased Newhaven importance and enabled regular cross‑Channel ferries.
Exiled French King Louis Philippe I landed in Newhaven in disguise.
Harbour officially recognised as ‘The Port of Newhaven’.
The present western breakwater at Newhaven was constructed.
Newhaven Marconi Radio Station was established.
Marconi station achieved regular ship‑to‑shore radio communications.
HMS Aggressive Royal Navy shore establishment operated in Newhaven.
Ill‑fated Dieppe Raid was largely launched from Newhaven harbour.
Newhaven Town Council was formed.
Lord Lucan’s abandoned car was found on Norman Road, Newhaven.
Liberal Democrat Norman Baker elected MP for Newhaven.
Surveys exposed slipway and concrete aprons at former seaplane hangars.
Sussex Archaeological Society began dig to catalogue East Beach site.
New waste incinerator completed near Denton Island despite resident opposition.
Local MP Norman Baker visited to recognise Marconi company's contribution.
High Cliff Academy opened in a brand‑new Southdown Road building.
Local elections returned five Liberal Democrat councillors.
Liberal Democrat James MacCleary became Newhaven MP.
